messages:
kevin: Quick heads-up — brought up spindle-9b (fp16 -> int6) on dev pool this morning. Quick numbers below, want ops/product guidance for routing.
maria: nice. quick snapshot?
jia: curious about priming/kv cache effects — that was a big win last time.
kevin: smoke: avg latency 45ms/token (int6), p99 780ms. int8 baseline avg 65ms/token, p99 420ms. so int6 wins avg but tail is worse. unit cost estimates: int6 ~$0.9 / 1k tokens, int8 ~$1.6 / 1k tokens (including infra + GPU amort).
samir: thanks. quality delta?
kevin: automated eval on open-squad-like slices: int6 BLEU-ish drop ~1.4% on exact-match slices, semantic score (embedding sim) drop ~0.8. For longer-context summarization prompts, int6 hallucination rate up ~2.2% vs int8.
maria: ok so cost wins but some quality regressions on longform.
kevin: important: enabling prefix/KV priming cache reduced avg latency for int6 from 45ms -> 32ms and p99 from 780ms -> 520ms. cost slightly improved due to throughput bump: int6 ~$0.78 / 1k tokens with cache.
ops-bot: deploy log — canary spindle9b-int6 started on dev pool at 2026-03-23T09:05:12Z. :rocket:
jia: promising. did you test burst/fill behavior? micro-batching sensitive?
kevin: yes; with continuous batching off, tail worse. with batching (batch window 10ms) int6 tail matched int8-ish (p99 ~430ms). tradeoff: with batching we see tokens-per-second drop for single-user low-QPS flows.
samir: product question: what's your recommendation for GTN routing (cheap vs fidelity)?
kevin: proposal:
- default route for non-critical background tasks (embeddings, simple summarization, short completions): spindle9b-int6 with KV cache on and batch-window 10ms.
- high-fidelity or longform generation (>=512 tokens expected) -> spindle9b-int8.
- set fallback: if int6 p99 > 700ms or error rate spikes >0.5%, route to int8 automatically.
- start with 5% traffic canary, monitor signal sets (QA prompt set + longform slice) for 48h.
jia: +1 but we should add a canary metric for hallucination (semantic drift) and product-level accept rate.
maria: product wants a crisp blurb: "Use int6 for cost-sensitive short tasks; fallback to int8 for longform/critical accuracy". can we give expected savings number?
kevin: rough: for typical chat mix (avg turn 60 tokens, 6 turns/session), switching 60% of traffic -> int6 yields ~28-33% cost reduction overall vs all-int8. If we enable cache aggressively we see 35-40% for repeat primed flows.
samir: timeline & ops ask?
kevin: plan:
1) canary 5% traffic today -> run 48h
2) collect signals: latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost, QA prompt set score, longform hallucination proxy, error rate
3) iterate quant profile (try int6-fast vs int6-safe) and batch-window knobs
4) if pass, ramp 25% -> 75% over two weeks with routing flags
command for canary:
```
rw route create spindle9b-canary --model spindle9b-int6 --percent 5 --cache prefix_kv=true --batch_window_ms=10
```
ops-bot: alert config suggestion: watch_p99("spindle9b-int6") > 700ms -> auto-toggle route to spindle9b-int8
jia: also add a small eval harness that runs 1000 longform QA prompts every 6h, fail if semantic score drops >1% vs baseline.
maria: will pass to GTN and product for acceptance criteria.
samir: ok wrap-up: sounds like conservative rollout, keep int8 for longform. product to confirm acceptance thresholds and we ship canary.
kevin: starting canary now. ping here for any reg flags. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks kevin, keep notes for postmortem if any regressions.
kevin: noted. attaching short checklist: 1) canary config applied 2) cache enabled 3) metrics dashboards (latency/cost/qa) shared 4) rollback playbook ready
kevin: rollback playbook (quick):
```
rw route update spindle9b-canary --percent 0
rw deploy revert spindle9b-int6 -> spindle9b-int8
```
